questions.question: Mohit and Rohit undertook a work for Rs. 2200. Mohit alone can do that work in 10 days and Rohit alone can do the same work in 12 days. If they work together, then what will be the difference in the amount they receive?
questions.solution:
Given: 

Mohit and Rohit undertook work for Rs. 2200.

Mohit alone can do that work in 10 days and Rohit alone can do the same work in 12 days.

Concept used:

Efficiency = (Total work / Total time taken)

Efficiency = work done in a single day 

The efficiency of a person is inversely proportional to the number of days to complete the work.

Calculation:

The ratio of the number of days to complete the work is,

10: 12 = 5: 6 

The efficiency ratio will be 6:5 

Money will be distributed as per their efficiency ratio

Money received by Mohit,

⇒ 2200 × 6 / 11 = Rs 1200

Money received by Rohit,

⇒ 2200 - 1200 = Rs 1000

Difference in their share,

⇒1200 - 1000 = Rs 200

**∴ The correct option is 2**

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 10 days and B can do it in 15 days. They work together for 2 days and then A leaves. How long will B take to finish the remaining work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can do a piece of work in 10 days.

B can do it in 15 days.

A and B work together for 2 days, then A leaves.

**Formula Used:**

Work done by A in 1 day = 1/10

Work done by B in 1 day = 1/15

Work done by A and B together in 1 day = 1/10 + 1/15

Work done by A and B together in 2 days = 2 × (1/10 + 1/15)

Remaining work = 1 - Work done by A and B in 2 days

Time taken by B to finish the remaining work = Remaining work / Work done by B in 1 day

**Calculation:**

Work done by A in 1 day = 1/10

Work done by B in 1 day = 1/15

Work done by A and B together in 1 day = 1/10 + 1/15

⇒ Work done by A and B together in 1 day = (3 + 2) / 30 = 5 / 30

⇒ Work done by A and B together in 1 day = 1/6

Work done by A and B together in 2 days = 2 × 1/6 = 2/6

⇒ Work done by A and B together in 2 days = 1/3

Remaining work = 1 - 1/3 = 2/3

Time taken by B to finish the remaining work = (2/3) / (1/15)

⇒ Time taken by B to finish the remaining work = (2/3) × 15/1

⇒ Time taken by B to finish the remaining work = 10 days

**B will take 10 days to finish the remaining work.**

questions.question: A and B can do a piece of work in 15 days, while B and C can do the same work in 12 days, and C and A in 10 days. They all work together for 5 days, and then B and C leave. How many days more will A take to finish the work?
questions.solution:
Given:

A and B can do a piece of work in 15 days, while B and C can do the same work in 12 days, and C and A in 10 days.

They all work together for 5 days, and then B and C leave.

Concept used:

Total Work = Work done each day × Total time taken (in days)

Calculation:

LCM (15, 12, 10) = 60

Let the total work be the LCM of the time taken by them.

Hence, total work = 60 units

Thus,

A & B together do each day = 60 ÷ 15 = 4 units

B & C together do each day = 60 ÷ 12 = 5 units

C & A together do each day = 60 ÷ 10 = 6 units

Hence,

A + B = 4 ....(1)

B + C = 5 ....(2)

C + A = 6 ....(3)

Now, 2(A + B + C) = 15 ....(4)

Solving these equations we get,

A = 2.5; B = 1.5; C = 3.5.

Now, in 5 days work done = 5 × (A + B + C) = 5 × 7.5 = 37.5 units

Remaining work = 60 - 37.5 = 22.5 work

Time taken by A to complete the work = 22.5 ÷ 2.5 = 9 days

**∴ Time taken by A to complete the work is 9 days.**

questions.question: A, B and C are Accountants. A alone can file a return in 6 hours and B alone can file the same return in 10 hours. All three together can do it in 3 hours. In what time will C alone file the same return?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work (LCM of 6, 10, 3) = 30 units.

Efficiency: A = 30/6 = 5; B = 30/10 = 3; (A+B+C) = 30/3 = 10.

Efficiency of C = Total Efficiency − (A + B) = 10 − (5 + 3) = 2 units/hr.

Time for C = Total Work ÷ Efficiency = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A = 6 hours

Time taken by B = 10 hours

Time taken by (A+B+C) = 3 hours

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Time taken × Efficiency

Reciprocal Rule

The combined rate of work is the sum of individual rates: 1/Tₜₒₜₐₗ = 1/TA + 1/TB + 1/TC.

Pipes and Cisterns

This concept is identical to Time & Work, where an outlet pipe is treated as having negative efficiency.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the work done by each person, which is the ratio of their efficiencies if they work for the same duration.</p

questions.question: A can do a piece of work alone in 40 days. A and B together can do the same work in 10 days. C is 50% less efficient than B. In how many days can A and C together complete the same work ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM of 40 and 10 = 40 units.

Efficiency of A = 40 ÷ 40 = 1 unit/day and Efficiency of (A + B) = 40 ÷ 10 = 4 units/day.

Efficiency of B = 4 − 1 = 3 units/day.

C is 50% less efficient than B ⇒ Efficiency of C = 50% of 3 = 1.5 units/day.

Time for (A + C) = Total work ÷ Combined Efficiency = 40 ÷ (1 + 1.5) = 40 ÷ 2.5 = 16 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A alone = 40 days

Time taken by A and B together = 10 days

C is 50% less efficient than B.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A

 A + B

⇒ Efficiency of B = Efficiency of (A + B) − Efficiency of A

⇒ Efficiency of B = 4 − 1 = 3 units/day

⇒ Since C is 50% less efficient than B, C's efficiency = 3 − (50% of 3) = 1.5 units/day

⇒ Combined efficiency of A and C = Efficiency of A + Efficiency of C

⇒ Combined efficiency of (A + C) = 1 + 1.5 = 2.5 units/day

⇒ Time taken by (A + C) = Total Work ÷ Combined efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 40 ÷ 2.5 = 400 ÷ 25 = 16 days

**∴ The correct answer is 16 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work and Time Relationship

Time and efficiency are inversely proportional to each other. Total work completed is strictly equal to the product of efficiency and the time taken.

Joint Efficiency Principle

When multiple people work together without obstructing one another, their combined efficiency is simply the sum of their individual efficiencies (e.g., EffA₊B = EffA + EffB).

Percentage Efficiency Change

When a person is x% less efficient than another, their new efficiency is calculated as Base Efficiency × (100 − x) ÷ 100.

questions.question: A can do a work in 20 days and B can do it in 14 days. If they work together for 7 days, then the fraction of the work left is:
questions.solution:
**Given**

A do work in 20 days

B do work in 14 days

**Concept used**

Total work = Efficiency × Number of days work

**Calculation**

let the total work is 140 units i.e. L.C.M of 20 and 14

A's one day work = 140/20

⇒ 7 units

B's one day work = 140/14

⇒10 units

work done by A and B in one day = 7 units + 10 units

⇒17 units

work done by A and B in seven days = 17 × 7

⇒ 119 units

work left = 140 - 119

⇒ 21 units

Fraction of the work left = 21/140

⇒ 3/20

**∴ The fraction of the work left is 3/20 **

questions.question: A man alone can paint a house in 9 day and a woman alone can paint the house in 18 days. If 3 men and 3 women worked together. then in how many day they will paint the house?
questions.solution:
**Given Data:**

Man paints in 9 days

Woman paints in 18 days

3 men and 3 women

**Concept:**

Use the concept of combined work rate.

**Solution:**

Man = 9

Women = 18

LCM = 18

Unit work by man = 2

Unit work by women = 1

Total work done by 3 men and 3 women = 3 × 2 + 3 × 1 = 9

Work done = 18/9 = 2 days.

**Therefore, they will paint the house in 2 days.**
